readme_content:
# Veyra ### Real-time GPU Video Enhancement for Windows **Super Resolution · Denoising · HDR · Frame Generation · Capture · PS5 / Xbox / PC Streaming** Turn local video, capture cards and game streaming into one real-time GPU enhancement pipeline.
[![GitHub Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo?style=for-the-badge&logo=github&label=Stars)](https://github.com/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo/stargazers) [![GitHub Forks](https://img.shields.io/github/forks/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo?style=for-the-badge&logo=github&label=Forks)](https://github.com/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo/network/members) [![Latest Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo?style=for-the-badge&logo=github&label=Release)](https://github.com/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo/releases/latest) [![Release Asset Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo/total?style=for-the-badge&logo=github&label=Release%20Downloads)](https://github.com/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo/releases) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo?style=for-the-badge&label=License)](LICENSE)
**79K+ cumulative Veyra portable-package downloads** (79,332 as of 2026-11-08) · **103K+ downloads across all GitHub Release assets** (103,337 including source archives, checksums and images). [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo/releases) · Counts are download events, not unique users.
[**⬇ Download Latest Release**](https://github.com/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo/releases/latest)   ·   [**📖 User Guide / Wiki**](https://github.com/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo/wiki)   ·   [**🇨🇳 简体中文**](README_CN.md)   ·   [**🐛 Report an Issue**](https://github.com/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo/issues)

One engine. Any source. Real-time enhancement.



⭐ Star History

Open source · GPL-3.0 · Windows 11 · C++ · DirectX 12 · NVIDIA & AMD

--- **2.1.2 update:** dual SR, SR-then-downsample, NVIDIA Low Latency, experimental RX 7000 NR and capture/FG/audio/volume fixes. [Full update and migration](docs/RELEASE_NOTES_2.1.2.md). **2.1.1 historical release, 2026-10-27:** processed-picture recording with audio,90° playback rotation, per-layer NR percentage controls and export sizing, event-driven refresh/VRR/HDR queries, AMD HDR+NR handling, AA ordering, capture timestamp handling, NR shutdown, popup layout, screenshots and fullscreen fixes. [All changes since2.1.0](docs/RELEASE_NOTES_2.1.1.md). **New-effect cost examples:** RTX5070 standard4K anti-aliasing fixtures: FXAA~0.15ms, SMAA/MLAA~0.30ms. Final single-face mesh beauty:1080p~0.93ms,4K~1.42ms. Costs vary with content/hardware; no local AMD speedup percentage was measured. [Conditions and limits](docs/history/releases/RELEASE_NOTES_2.1.0.md). **📖 [English User Guide / GitHub Wiki](https://github.com/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo/wiki)** — installation, software setup, capture card compatibility, troubleshooting, and community-tested solutions. [中文知识库（飞书）](https://qcnv4i7tnd7l.feishu.cn/wiki/space/7688258025282358221?ccm_open_type=lark_wiki_spaceLink&open_tab_from=wiki_home). **2.1.6:** Instant replay/F9, microphone mixing/separate tracks, all-effect exclusion, VFR dedup/60→30 and presentation/logging repairs, refined flow, updated defaults and collapsed HDR controls. [All changes and measured data](docs/RELEASE_NOTES_2.1.6.md). ANR host source is included; its runtime is not distributed. **2.1.5:** Smoother frame pacing after capture deduplication and preview correction for invalid capture timestamps. [Full changes](docs/RELEASE_NOTES_2.1.5.md). **2.1.4:** Optional VB-CABLE capture audio, DLSS/FSR/RTX dual super resolution, NVIDIA DLAA, HDR wide-gamut restoration, NR inference reuse, 1% low FPS, and recording and compatibility fixes. [Full changes and settings migration](docs/RELEASE_NOTES_2.1.4.md). **2.1.3:** Three RTX Video SR families and independent second-pass models, medium defaults, inline NR web/list editing, RTX30 VFG compatibility, RX7000 multi-GPU and seeking/menu fixes. [Full changes, comparison and migration](docs/RELEASE_NOTES_2.1.3.md). ## Highlights **2.0.4 NR controls:** each NR layer's **Enhancement delta → Total strength** now reaches 5. **Picture control** defaults off; enable it and select Automatic or Manual. Automatic values now adapt separately to styles 0/1/2, with an amount slider (0 retains raw strength, 1 applies full correction). The nine manual controls cover hue, chroma, neutral tint, source color retention, lightness retention, shadows, highlights, local compression and temporal stability. **Use this style’s automatic values** provides a manual starting point. Switching modes keeps manual values; turning control off preserves the original residual algorithm. Five extrapolates one inference's residual, and protection reduces the corresponding changes; it cannot promise full gain five with no artifacts on every video. Presets, List/Node sessions, PNGs and video exports share the settings. [Local validation and known limits](docs/history/reports/NR_STRENGTH_PROTECTION_EXECUTION_2026-10-05.md). - **Rebuilt interface:** Home, Cinema, Professional List, Nodes, Colour, Export and Settings; Simplified/Traditional Chinese, English and Japanese. - **Node editing and layered NR:** executable connections, independent NR/colour parameters, separate List/Node configurations, sessions and presets. - **PC / Xbox streaming:** Moonlight/Sunshine-compatible PC streaming and unofficial experimental Xbox support, alongside PS5, capture cards and screen capture. - **New export workflow:** editable ordered queue, trimming, MP4/MKV, multiple audio/embedded subtitle tracks, cancellation/retry and completion sound. - **Enhancement and compatibility:** SF310.9.16 performance/legacy models, NVIDIA original for RTX50 and AMD lmxxf, DLSS/XeSS/FSR options, capture improvements and a persistent OBS Game Capture switch with restart confirmation. Full details are in the Release. **Current version: [2.1.6](https://github.com/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo/releases/tag/v2.1.6)** · [Full bilingual update](docs/RELEASE_NOTES_2.1.6.md). ## New in 2.1.2 - **SR:** true dual RTX Video SR with separate second-pass controls, plus SR-then-downsample; ordinary 8K retained, new graphs check VRAM budget. - **GPU options:** NVIDIA Low Latency Off / On / On + Boost; experimental RX 7000 RedDuke NR, Small/Original and per-layer scale; separate RX 9000 path retained. - **FG:** sparse-noise-tolerant full-frame dedup, remove coarse generated-frame discard, smoothed anchors, optional VFG regulation, adaptive VSync capacity wait capped at 3 ms. - **Capture/audio:** WGC high-refresh cadence, ready-immediate no-FG capture, first-copy 60→30, Dolby/DTS carriers on generic PCM pins. - **Controls:** F7 screenshot / F8 recording in game mode too; Cinema volume dragging, endpoints, Enter/click-away confirmation and focus. [All changes since 2.1.1, measurements and migration](docs/RELEASE_NOTES_2.1.2.md) · [Build and corresponding source](docs/BUILD_2.1.2.md). ## New in 2.1.1 - **Interface and SR defaults:** software UI drawing by default, an optional GPU renderer with restart confirmation, and RTX Video SR high as the new SR model selection; saved model choices are retained. - **Record and rotate:** record the processed picture with player audio; rotate playback90° in Cinema/Professional with matching preview and window layout. - **NR sizing:** per-layer25–100% scale controls, saved presets/sessions and fixed/percentage video-export inference sizes with independent output resolution. - **Display and frame generation:** background event-driven refresh/VRR/HDR queries, shared signal-panel refresh and HDR-cache recovery. - **Enhancement:** correct AMD FSR-off state, native-HDR NR proxy/reconstruction and List-mode AA placement after NR. - **Interaction and lifecycle:** popup first-open layout, real screenshot paths/formats, fullscreen/maximized restoration, playlist key ownership, capture preparation timestamps and NR/NVAPI teardown. [Full2.1.1 update](docs/RELEASE_NOTES_2.1.1.md) · [Build and corresponding source](docs/BUILD_2.1.1.md). ## New in 2.1.0 - **AMD NR0.44:** RX9000 Small/Original models via the per-layer performance switch(default on), saved in presets/sessions/export; explicit asset errors, no new RX6000/7000 support. - **Anti-aliasing:** independent FXAA/SMAA/MLAA, List/Nodes, quality/strength controls, HDR and List export; experimental temporal SMAA defaults off. - **Beauty and original-face restoration:** separate switches, up to six layers,468-point contours, eye/brow/lip exclusion, per-frame detection and smoothing; restoration mixes the pre-effect source back into faces. - **Capture modes:** native enumeration fallback, driver ranges/steps/custom-size checks, searchable legacy list, exact rate/pixel-format matching, explicit substitution rejection, saved/resumed capture settings. - **Network and AVerMedia audio:** shared buffering/reconnect, slow-server buffering status, HLS/interlaced damage handling, throttled subtitle scanning; vendor multichannel audio, non-PCM confirmation, complete-payload decode and bounded recovery. - **Other fixes:** game-mode handoff/hotkeys/scaling/static resize, fullscreen transport/cursor, disabled-node order and export protocol consistency, home/sponsor page, corrected Bilibili profile and complete new translations. [Complete2.0.9→2.1.0 update, instructions and validation limits](docs/history/releases/RELEASE_NOTES_2.1.0.md). The exact user-tested packages are promoted without rebuilding/repacking; internal2.1.0-test labels/manifests remain, PE2.1.0.0. ## Install and upgrade Download **Veyra-2.1.6-NVIDIA-win64-portable.zip** or **Veyra-2.1.6-AMD-win64-portable.zip** for Veyra's active GPU. Extract with Windows or 7-Zip into a new writable folder and run **veyra_qml_ui.exe**. You need one GPU package to run the application; source assets are only for rebuilding. Windows 11 x64 and DirectX 12 are required; Qt and approved runtimes are included, while GPU/capture drivers are installed separately. Backend hardware requirements vary; most local tests used an RTX 5070. Start with effects off, check picture/sound, then enable effects individually. High resolution, layered NR and frame generation increase GPU/VRAM requirements. **The 1.4.4 UI guide is obsolete.** Version 2.0 uses separate settings. Retain the old version for rollback; do not overwrite the new package with old `veyra.ini`, an entire `runtime_local` folder or mixed DLLs. **Upgrade 2.1.1→2.1.2:** prefer extracting into a new folder; copy only `runtime_local/user-data-2.0.0` and custom `runtime_local/luts` after closing Veyra. Use Settings→About for custom paths. Same-flavour in-place overlay is possible after exit but leaves stale components. [Steps](docs/RELEASE_NOTES_2.1.2.md#升级并保留设置). **Historical 2.1.0→2.1.1 migration:** close Veyra and back up user data first. Overlay the matching GPU package contents into the existing executable directory to retain its data folder. For a new installation directory on the same PC, open Settings→About→User data in the old version, then close it and copy its `user-data-2.0.0` folder into the new package’s `runtime_local` directory. Copy only the data folder to keep the new runtime files; custom data-directory launches

name: agent-skills
description: Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents.
readme_content:
# Agent Skills **Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents.** Skills encode the workflows, quality gates, and best practices that senior engineers use when building software. These ones are packaged so AI agents follow them consistently across every phase of development. ![Addy's Agent Skills](https://addyosmani.com/assets/images/addys-agent-skills.jpg) ``` DEFINE PLAN BUILD VERIFY REVIEW SHIP ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ │ Idea │ ───▶ │ Spec │ ───▶ │ Code │ ───▶ │ Test │ ───▶ │ QA │ ───▶ │ Go │ │Refine│ │ PRD │ │ Impl │ │Debug │ │ Gate │ │ Live │ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ /spec /plan /build /test /review /ship ``` --- ## Commands 9 slash commands that map to the development lifecycle. Each one activates the right skills automatically. | What you're doing | Command | Key principle | |-------------------|---------|---------------| | Define what to build | `/spec` | Spec before code | | Plan how to build it | `/plan` | Small, atomic tasks | | Build incrementally | `/build` | One slice at a time | | Prove it works | `/test` | Tests are proof | | Set the quality bar | `/constraints` | Decide it once, enforce it everywhere | | Review before merge | `/review` | Improve code health | | Audit web performance | `/webperf` | Measure before you optimize | | Simplify the code | `/code-simplify` | Clarity over cleverness | | Ship to production | `/ship` | Faster is safer | In Claude Code these install as plugin commands. Where a built-in command has the same name, as `/review` does, use the namespaced form: `/agent-skills:review`. Want fewer manual steps once the spec exists? **`/build auto`** generates the plan and implements every task in a single approved pass — you approve the plan once, then it runs autonomously. It removes the human stepping *between* tasks, not the verification: every task is still test-driven and committed individually, and it pauses on failures or risky steps. Skills also activate automatically based on what you're doing — designing an API triggers `api-and-interface-design`, building UI triggers `frontend-ui-engineering`, and so on. --- ## Quick Start **Fastest path — any agent, one command.** The open [skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) installs into 70+ agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Cline, and more): ```bash npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills # install all 25 skills npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --list # browse before installing ``` Or grab individual skills: ```bash npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --skill code-review-and-quality # five-axis review before merge npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --skill interview-me # requirements interrogation, one question at a time npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --skill test-driven-development # red-green-refactor, enforced ``` > **Installing one skill?** A per-skill `npx` install copies only > `skills//`, not the repo-level `references/` directory. The skill still > works, but paths to supplementary shared checklists are unavailable. Use a > whole-repo integration, clone the repository, or copy the needed checklist into > a `references/` directory inside the installed skill. This portability gap is > tracked in [#361](https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills/issues/361). Prefer a native integration? Pick your tool below.
Claude Code (recommended) **Marketplace install:** ``` /plugin marketplace add addyosmani/agent-skills /plugin install agent-skills@addy-agent-skills ``` > **SSH errors?** The marketplace clones repos via SSH. If you don't have SSH keys set up on GitHub, either [add your SSH key](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/connecting-to-github-with-ssh/adding-a-new-ssh-key-to-your-github-account) or use the full HTTPS URL to force HTTPS cloning during the marketplace-add step: > ```bash > /plugin marketplace add https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git > /plugin install agent-skills@addy-agent-skills > ``` > > If `/plugin install` still fails with `git@github.com: Permission denied (publickey)` on Windows or macOS, the recommended workaround is to configure Git once to rewrite GitHub SSH URLs to HTTPS for subprocess clones: > ```bash > git config --global url."https://github.com/".insteadOf git@github.com: > ``` **Local / development:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git claude --plugin-dir /path/to/agent-skills ```
Cursor Put workflow skills under `.cursor/skills/` (sync from `agent-skills/skills/`) and short policies in `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` — do not paste full skills into rules. Both directories live in your project; this repo does not ship a `.cursor/` folder. See [docs/cursor-setup.md](docs/cursor-setup.md).
Antigravity CLI Install as a native plugin for skills and subagents. In affected Antigravity CLI releases, legacy command TOMLs are reported as converted but their wrapper commands are not discoverable; invoke the underlying namespaced skills directly. See [docs/antigravity-setup.md](docs/antigravity-setup.md#lifecycle-workflows-and-command-compatibility). **Install from the repo:** ```bash agy plugin install https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git ``` **Install from a local clone:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git agy plugin install ./agent-skills ```
Gemini CLI Install as native skills for auto-discovery, or add to `GEMINI.md` for persistent context. See [docs/gemini-cli-setup.md](docs/gemini-cli-setup.md). **Install from the repo:** ```bash gemini skills install https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git --path skills ``` **Install from a local clone:** ```bash gemini skills install ./agent-skills/skills/ ```
Windsurf Add skill contents to your Windsurf rules configuration. See [docs/windsurf-setup.md](docs/windsurf-setup.md).
OpenCode Copy skills to `.opencode/skills/` (or `~/.config/opencode/skills/`), add a project-local `AGENTS.md`, and use the built-in `skill` tool for agent-driven execution. Optional slash commands can be added under `.opencode/commands/`. See [docs/opencode-setup.md](docs/opencode-setup.md).
GitHub Copilot Use agent definitions from `agents/` as Copilot personas and skill content in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`. The lifecycle slash commands (`/spec`, `/plan`, `/build`, `/test`, `/review`, `/ship`) are Claude Code commands and do not appear in Copilot; invoke the skills by name (`/spec-driven-development`, …) instead. See [docs/copilot-setup.md](docs/copilot-setup.md). Using the standalone `copilot` CLI? Install it as a plugin — see [docs/copilot-cli-setup.md](docs/copilot-cli-setup.md).
Kiro IDE & CLI Skills for Kiro reside under ".kiro/skills/" and can be stored under Project or Global level. Kiro also supports Agents.md. See Kiro docs at https://kiro.dev/docs/skills/
Codex Install as a native Codex plugin (Codex CLI v0.122+): ```bash codex plugin marketplace add addyosmani/agent-skills codex plugin add agent-skills@agent-skills ``` The first command registers the marketplace; the second installs the plugin. Codex reads the root `skills/` directory directly through `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`. Once installed, invoke skills in chat using `@` (e.g., `@spec-driven-development`). See [docs/codex-setup.md](docs/codex-setup.md) for local installation and troubleshooting.
Command Code Install natively with the built-in `cmd skills` command. Command Code clones the repo, discovers every `SKILL.md`, and installs into `.commandcode/skills/`: ```bash cmd skills add addyosmani/agent-skills # pick skills to install (project) cmd skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --global # install for all projects (~/.commandcode/skills/) cmd skills add addyosmani/agent-skills -s spec-driven-development # install a specific skill ``` Installed skills show up in the TUI slash menu, e.g. `/spec-driven-development`. See [docs/commandcode-setup.md](docs/commandcode-setup.md).
Other Agents Skills are plain Markdown - they work with any agent that accepts system prompts or instruction files. See [docs/getting-started.md](docs/getting-started.md). Hosts that install the pack but aren't listed above are in [docs/other-hosts.md](docs/other-hosts.md).
--- ## Adoption Already installed? How you roll the pack out depends on your codebase. The **[Adoption Guide](docs/adoption-guide.md)** covers two paths: the full lifecycle from day one for a greenfield project, or an incremental, verification-first rollout for an established codebase. --- ## All 25 Skills The commands above are entry points. The pack includes 25 skills total — 24 lifecycle skills plus the `using-agent-skills` meta-skill. Each skill is a structured workflow with steps, verification gates, and anti-rationalization tables. You can also reference any skill directly. ### Meta - Discover which skill applies | Skill | What It Does | Use When | |-------|-------------|----------| | [using-agent-skills](skills/using-agent-skills/SKILL.md) | Maps incoming work to the right skill workflow and defines shared operating rules | Starting a session or deciding which skill applies | ### Define - Clarify what to build | Skill | What It Does | Use When | |-------|-------------|----------| | [interview-me](skills/interview-me/SKILL.md) | One-question-at-a-time interview that extracts what the user actually wants instead of what they think they should want, until ~95% confidence | The ask is underspecified, or the user invokes "interview me" / "grill me" | | [idea-refine](skills/idea-refine/SKILL.md) | Structured divergent/convergent thinking to turn vague ideas into concrete proposals | You have a rough concept that needs exploration | | [spec-driven-development](skills/spec-driven-development/SKILL.md) | Write a PRD covering objectives, commands, structure, code style, testing, and boundaries before any code | Starting a new project, feature, or significant change | | [constraint-driven-development](skills/constraint-driven-development/SKILL.md) | Interviews you for a quality bar with sane default thresholds, writes CONSTRAINTS.md, places each check by cost, and catches agents silencing checks or skipping tests to get green | No standards are written down, or an agent is producing more than anyone reads | ### Plan - name: plannotator
description: The workspace to stay in the loop and on top of agents - shape, decide, plan, annotate, review code, share with team, and send all feedback to agents with one click.
readme_content:
Everything you need to annotate and stay in the loop with your agents
Inbox Surface • Artifacts • Code Review
Annotate plans, specs, markdown, HTML, and other interactive artifacts. Review diffs and PRs. Send feedback to your agent.

                       

Plannotator Inbox · Official site · Code Review · Visual HTML Skills · Herdr Annotate · (Legacy) Plan Mode

# Plannotator **⭐️ NEW:** [Plannotator Inbox](https://plannotator.ai/inbox/) is the missing review layer between you and multi-agent work. It surfaces decisions, prototypes, variations, plans, and everything you need to stay in the loop. Works with all coding agents and personal assistants. Plannotator is a local, browser-based review surface for AI coding agents: Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kiro, Droid, Amp, DeepSeek Harness, and Pi. Plannotator Inbox also works with personal assistants (Grok Bot, Muse, Hermes, OpenClaw). **It plugs directly into your agent** through plugins, hooks and commands. When the agent proposes a decision, plan, html, or finishes working, the app opens in your browser and you mark it up, comment, and send feedback directly to the agent for it to act on it.
### Review documents, plans, and agent messages Annotate plans, specs, messages, html, then send the feedback to your agent.

Demo: Plan review with Pi
### Code Review Review local changes or remote PRs. Comment on diffs, suggest code. Your comments go back to the agent. Works with Git, GitButler, Jujutsu (`jj`), Perforce (`p4`), GitHub, and GitLab.

AI built in: ask AI about anything you're reviewing,
or launch AI reviews that post comments to the diff.

## Annotate HTML Artifacts

## Plannotator Inbox

The Plannotator Inbox is one local window where your agents leave you messages, questions, files, and guided reviews while they keep working. Answer a question with a click, annotate a file, and press Send when you can. Nothing holds an agent session open while you do, and your reply goes back to the session that asked. ``` plannotator inbox ``` Claude Code, Pi, and OpenCode connect through Plannotator's plugins, and your replies arrive as their next turn. Any other agent reaches it over MCP with `plannotator inbox mcp`, and `plannotator inbox --help` is the guide an agent reads. [Watch the demo](https://plannotator.ai/assets/inbox-film.mp4) · [More on the Inbox](https://plannotator.ai/inbox/) · [Docs](https://plannotator.ai/docs/reference/inbox/) ## Herdr Annotate: Plannotator in the Terminal

  

[Herdr Annotate](https://github.com/plannotator/herdr-annotate) brings Plannotator-style review to the terminal: annotate terminal text, review whole Markdown documents and your coding agent's replies inside [Herdr](https://herdr.dev), and send the feedback straight back to the agent as its next message. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Copilot CLI, and Droid replies. Annotations are saved in the Plannotator data directory, so terminal reviews and app reviews compound. ``` herdr plugin install plannotator/herdr-annotate ``` Prefer it standalone? [Plannotator TUI](https://github.com/plannotator/plannotator-tui) powers the document review and runs without Herdr: `brew install plannotator/tap/plannotator-tui`. --- ## Commands On Codex, swap the slash commands for `!plannotator …` (e.g. `!plannotator review`) or the `$plannotator-*` skills. ### Annotate ``` /plannotator-annotate README.md # Local markdown file /plannotator-annotate src/ # Browse and annotate files in a folder /plannotator-annotate https://docs.rs/… # Fetch and annotate any URL /plannotator-annotate report.html --render-html # Render HTML as-is instead of converting /plannotator-last # Annotate the agent's last message ``` Need a realistic document to try? Copy the [product requirements document template and filled example](https://docs.plannotator.ai/templates/product-requirements-document) as Markdown. ### Code review ``` /plannotator-review # Review uncommitted changes /plannotator-review # Review a GitHub pull request /plannotator-review # Review a GitLab merge request plannotator review --gitbutler # Review an active GitButler workspace plannotator review --patch-file reading.diff # Review a static caller-supplied unified diff ``` GitButler users can review the whole workspace, one stack, or one branch layer. See the [GitButler workflow guide](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/workflows/gitbutler). ### Plan mode No command needed. Plan mode is wired in through each harness's hooks. Any time your agent creates a plan, the markdown review surface opens for you. ### CLI ``` plannotator sessions # List active Plannotator sessions plannotator sessions --open 1 # Reopen a session in the browser plannotator archive # Browse saved plan decisions read-only ``` --- ## Privacy and network behavior Plannotator does not collect usage telemetry or analytics. Plans, diffs, annotations, drafts, history, and configuration stay local by default. Each plan review, annotate, archive, share-portal, and code-review app surface checks GitHub for the latest Plannotator release when it loads. This sends no plan or review content and gives the Plannotator project owner no usage analytics, although GitHub receives an ordinary request. There is currently no opt-out setting for the release check. Local Git code review can also query the configured `origin` with `git ls-remote` to detect the default branch and a stale baseline; it does not send the local diff. That remote query runs when the review opens, when the page loads its diff, when you switch the diff type or base (including the "Diff out of date · Refresh" button), and when you press Fetch — never on a timer, so an idle review page makes no network calls. Turn it off entirely with `plannotator review --no-git-remote-check`, `PLANNOTATOR_GIT_REMOTE_CHECK=0`, or `{ "gitRemoteCheck": false }` in `~/.plannotator/config.json`; the compare target then comes from local refs only and the "behind GitHub" banner never appears. Content leaves the local workflow only when a network feature needs it: - URL annotation fetches the requested site, through Jina Reader by default for public pages or directly when Jina is disabled or unavailable. - GitHub and GitLab review uses your authenticated CLI and Git remote to retrieve PR or MR data. - Ask AI and review agents send the selected question and relevant plan, document, repository, or diff context to your configured provider. When Ask AI is answered by the agent session that opened Plannotator ("Ask this session"), the question goes to that session instead. - Sharing sends the complete link to whoever or whatever service you use to deliver it. Encrypted short links upload ciphertext to the paste service. - Workspaces is a separate hosted product, so the open source app's local-storage model does not apply to content placed there. The [privacy policy](https://plannotator.ai/privacy) documents these boundaries and the hosted website and waitlist data. --- ## Link sharing Open source asynchronous link sharing remains available for compatibility but is moving to deprecated support. Workspaces is the primary direction for team sharing. No removal date has been announced.

Legacy link-sharing demo: room.plannotator.ai

Share a plan with a teammate and they can annotate it themselves. Import their feedback and send it straight back to your agent. **Small markdown shares** are compressed into the URL fragment. The fragment is not included in the browser's request to the share portal, but it is not encrypted. Anyone or any messaging service with the complete link can read the shared content. The portal host still receives ordinary request metadata. **Large markdown and raw HTML shares** use a short-link service. The share payload is encrypted with AES-256-GCM before upload, the server stores only ciphertext, and the key is kept in the URL fragment rather than sent in the paste request. Anyone with the complete link can decrypt it. Hosted pastes expire after 7 days. Same model as [PrivateBin](https://privatebin.info/). The paste service is [self-hostable](https://docs.plan

description: Use Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, VSCode, Pi, and OpenCode (and 6 other harnesses) for free (1.3B+ free tokens) from your terminal, app, IDE, or phone, and now from the browser with native browser sessions (multi-harness + multi-model) like OpenClaw (voice supported + ToS friendly)
readme_content:
[![License: AGPL v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-AGPL_v3-2e7d32.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/Alishahryar1/free-claude-code/blob/main/LICENSE) [![Python 3.14](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.14-3776ab.svg?style=for-the-badge&logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![Package Manager: uv](assets/package-manager-uv.svg)](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv) [![Testing: Pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/Testing-Pytest-ad1457.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/Alishahryar1/free-claude-code/actions/workflows/tests.yml) [![Type Checker: Ty](https://img.shields.io/badge/Type%20Checker-ty-fdd835.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://pypi.org/project/ty/) [![Formatter: Ruff](https://img.shields.io/badge/Formatter-ruff-bf4b00.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) [![Logging: Loguru](https://img.shields.io/badge/logging-loguru-00695c.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/Delgan/loguru) [Quick Start](#quick-start) · [Providers](#choose-a-provider) · [Clients](#connect-your-client) · [Integrations](#optional-integrations) · [Manage](#manage-your-installation)

Independent open-source project. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. Claude and Claude Code are trademarks of Anthropic.

## Features - Route any supported harness to models from any supported provider. - 12 supported harnesses: [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview), [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex), [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi), [OpenCode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode), [Cline](https://github.com/cline/cline), [Hermes](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent), [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness), [Grok Build](https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build), [Muse Code](https://research.meta.ai/blog/introducing-muse-code-and-muse-spark-1-2/), [Aider](https://aider.chat/), [Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/docs/getting-started/), or [VS Code Chat](https://code.visualstudio.com/). - Preserved native streaming, tool use, and interleaved thinking for maximum performance. - For Claude Code, route [Fable](https://www.anthropic.com/claude/fable), [Opus](https://www.anthropic.com/claude/opus), [Sonnet](https://www.anthropic.com/claude/sonnet), and [Haiku](https://www.anthropic.com/claude/haiku) to supported models. - 61 supported providers, including free, paid, subscription, and local providers. - 1.3B+ free tokens per month. - FCC follows provider TOS and removes integrations if they stop being allowed. - Use through the terminal, desktop apps ([Codex App](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app), [Claude Desktop](https://claude.ai/download), and [DeepSeek Desktop](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)), IDE extensions ([VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/) and [JetBrains](https://www.jetbrains.com/)), your phone ([Discord](https://discord.com/) and [Telegram](https://telegram.org/)), or your browser through native Code sessions. - Voice notes supported for Discord and Telegram using local [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper) or [NVIDIA NIM](https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/speech/latest/asr/deploy-asr-models/whisper.html). - Up to 90% lower token usage using [RTK](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk) and [Headroom](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom). - State-of-the-art reliability features so you can keep coding through provider outages: - Automatic retries. - Configurable rate limits. - Configurable concurrency control. - Automatic model/provider fallback. - Automatic multi-API key fallback. Free-tier availability and limits are controlled by each provider and may change.

Claude Code running with FCC.

A native Codex session in FCC's browser UI.

## Quick Start ### 1. Install macOS/Linux: ```bash curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Alishahryar1/free-claude-code/main/scripts/install.sh" | sh ``` Windows PowerShell: ```powershell & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Alishahryar1/free-claude-code/main/scripts/install.ps1"))) ``` When prompted, choose at least one coding agent and optionally enable [RTK](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk) + [Headroom](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom) token optimization for supported agents. ### 2. Start FCC #### Windows Open **Free Claude Code** from your desktop or Start menu. #### macOS Open **Free Claude Code** from your desktop or Applications folder. #### Linux Run: ```bash fcc-server ``` FCC opens the Admin UI after starting. On Windows and macOS, use the tray or menu-bar icon to open Admin, restart, or quit. When using `fcc-server`, keep its terminal open. ### 3. Configure NVIDIA NIM 1. Create an API key at [build.nvidia.com/settings/api-keys](https://build.nvidia.com/settings/api-keys). 2. Open the Admin UI URL from the server log. 3. Open NVIDIA NIM in **Providers**, click **Add key**, paste the key, and click **Save**. 4. Leave `MODEL` on the default `nvidia_nim/nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b`, or search the model dropdown and select another model. 5. Click **Apply** to save your model selection. To protect the local proxy with a bearer token, enable **Proxy Authentication** in Admin.
### 4. Run Your Coding Agent Claude Code: ```bash fcc-claude ``` Codex: ```bash fcc-codex ``` Pi: ```bash fcc-pi ``` OpenCode 2: ```bash fcc-opencode ``` Cline: ```bash fcc-cline ``` Hermes: ```bash fcc-hermes ``` DeepSeek Harness Web: ```bash fcc-dsh ``` Grok Build: ```bash fcc-grok ``` Muse Code: ```bash fcc-muse ``` Aider: ```bash fcc-aider ``` Antigravity CLI (connect on the Integrations page first): ```bash fcc-agy ``` Other Chat Completions clients can use FCC's server URL followed by `/v1` as their OpenAI-compatible base URL (default `http://127.0.0.1:8082/v1`). Select an FCC model such as `gemini/models/gemini-3.5-flash-lite`. If Proxy Authentication is enabled, use its token as the client's API key. Both streaming and JSON replies are supported.

Select an FCC model from Claude Code's native /model picker.

[project.optional-dependencies]

    "transformers>=5.22.2",
    "accelerate>=1.15.0",
    "librosa>=1.0.0",
]

source = "vcs"

[tool.hatch.build]

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "pytorch-cu130"
url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130"
explicit = true

[dependency-groups]

    # pytest 9.2 breaks xdist provider grouping: pytest-dev/pytest#15303.
    "pytest>=9.1.1,<9.2",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.4.1.post1",
    "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",
    "ty>=0.0.99",
    "ruff>=0.17.4",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.8.0",
    "pytest-playwright>=0.10.0",

]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
line-ending = "auto"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]

addopts = "-p e2e.thread_diagnostics -n auto --dist=worksteal"

]

markers = [
    "live: opt-in local smoke tests that can touch real services",
    "interactive: smoke tests requiring manual user interaction",
    "provider: live provider checks",
    "messaging: live messaging p

name: buzz
description: A hive mind communication platform
readme_content:
Buzz 🐝

A workspace where humans and agents build together, on a relay you own.

Vision · Sovereign · Forge · Agents · Architecture · Releasing · Apache 2.0

People and agents building together in the same room.

--- ## What is this, really? Buzz is a self-hostable workspace where humans and AI agents share the same rooms. A Buzz **community** is the workspace a user reaches by URL. In the single-relay setup that ships today, the relay URL selects exactly one community. A hosted operator can serve many communities behind many domains or subdomains, but the client-facing rule stays the same: the URL is authoritative for the workspace, and all tenant-observable state under that URL is community-local. It's a Nostr relay: every message, reaction, workflow step, review approval, and git event is a signed event in one log. Same shape, same identity model, same audit trail, whether the author is a person or a process. In practice it feels like a team workspace. Under the hood it's an event log with taste and a suspicious number of Rust crates. Yes, it's another AI-adjacent developer tool. We're sorry. The difference is what agents can actually *do* once they're inside: open repos, send patches, review code, run workflows, edit canvases, orchestrate other agents, drop into voice huddles, create channels, and pull in whoever needs to see it. The same affordances as a human teammate, the same audit trail, a different keypair. --- ## Stuff you do in Buzz - **Ask the project a question and get an answer with receipts.** Agents search six months of history and post the threads, not vibes. - **Let an agent triage a bug without giving it the keys to the kingdom.** Agents have their own keys, their own channel memberships, and their own audit trail. Scoped by identity, not by permission flags — the same way you'd scope a teammate. - **Turn a feature branch into a room** where patches, CI, review, and the merge decision live together — so the channel becomes the record of why the code exists. - **Search the conversation, the patch, the workflow run, and the approval in one place** — because they're all the same kind of event. - **Let an agent run the workspace, not just talk in it.** Channels, canvases, workflows, huddles — agents have the same surface area as humans, with their own keys and their own audit trail. --- ## Where to find things Buzz's open-source code lives in two repositories. The desktop app has its own; the relay and the mobile client are here. | Component | Home | |---|---| | Desktop app | [block/buzz-app](https://github.com/block/buzz-app) | | Mobile client (iOS + Android) | This repo, in [`mobile/`](mobile/) | | Relay | This repo, in [`crates/buzz-relay/`](crates/buzz-relay/) | --- ## A look inside

Agents are members, not bots. Add an agent to a channel the same way you add a person.
Spin up a room in seconds. Name it, describe it, make it private.

Media you can talk about. Leave comments pinned to specific frames.
--- ## Why Buzz is better One community. One identity model. One event log. Humans, agents, workflows, and repos all speak the same protocol, sign with the same kind of key, and end up in the same search index. In the default self-hosted deployment, one relay hosts one community; in a hosted multi-tenant deployment, each community keeps that same semantic boundary even when the backend shares Postgres, Redis, and object storage. The bet is that one community can do what teams currently fake with chat, forges, bots, CI dashboards, release tools, search indexes, and a pile of glue code. Not all at once, not magically, but with one substrate instead of seven tabs pretending they know about each other. Agents are part of the room, not haunted cron jobs. --- ## Three little stories **Incident memory.** It's 2am. You type *"have we seen this error before?"* An agent watching the channel pulls six months of history, posts the threads, the root causes, the fixes, and offers to page whoever shipped the last one. The whole exchange — question, answer, evidence — stays in the channel. **Branch as room.** You open a feature branch. A channel appears. Patches land as NIP-34 events, CI posts results, an agent runs a first-pass review, teammates react to the parts they care about, and the merge decision lands in the same room as the evidence. **A release that writes itself.** A workflow fires on a tag. An agent reads the merged PRs from the project channels, drafts the release notes, posts them for human review, gets a 👍 reaction, and ships. Every step signed. Every step searchable. --- ## Works today · Being wired up · Strong opinions, pending code | ✅ Works today | 🚧 Being wired up | 💭 Strong opinions, pending code | |---|---|---| | Relay, channels, threads, DMs, canvases, media, search, audit log | Mobile clients (iOS + Android, Flutter) | Web-of-trust reputation across relays | | Desktop app (in [block/buzz-app](https://github.com/block/buzz-app)) | Workflow approval gates (infra exists, glue still drying) | Push notifications | | `buzz-cli` (agent-first, JSON in / JSON out) + ACP harness (Goose, Codex, Claude Code) | Huddle lifecycle events | Culture features | | YAML workflows: message / reaction / schedule / webhook triggers | | | | Git events (NIP-34: patches, repo announcements, status) | | | | Git hosting backend | | | Please do not plan your compliance program around the 💭 column yet. The VISION docs are the long version of what we think this becomes. --- ## Getting started New to Buzz? Pick the path that matches you. ### I just want to try the app The desktop app lives in [block/buzz-app](https://github.com/block/buzz-app). Head there to install, build, or run it. Need a relay for it to connect to? Deploy a hosted one, or follow **Quick start** below to stand one up locally. ### I want my own hosted relay To run a relay for your team without managing servers, you can deploy one to Railway in a click: [![Deploy on Railway](https://railway.com/button.svg)](https://railway.com/deploy/buzz-relay-block) See [here](https://engineering.block.xyz/blog/run-your-own-buzz-relay) for details. ### I want to run the relay from source See **Quick start** below — this is the developer / self-host path. ### I want to work on the mobile app The Flutter client is in [`mobile/`](mobile/). See [mobile/README.md](mobile/README.md) for setup and run instructions. --- ## Quick start This stands up the relay locally. For the desktop app, see [block/buzz-app](https://github.com/block/buzz-app); for the mobile app, see [mobile/README.md](mobile/README.md). You'll need [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) and [Hermit](https://cashapp.github.io/hermit/) (or Rust 1.88+, Node 24+, pnpm 10+, `just`). **Once:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/block/buzz.git && cd buzz . ./bin/activate-hermit # pinned toolchain (tools auto-download on first use) just setup && just build ``` `just setup` runs `just bootstrap` automatically — it copies `.env.example` to `.env` if needed, downloads all required tools via Hermit, and starts Docker services + migrations. **Every day:** ```bash . ./bin/activate-hermit just relay # starts the relay (and its Docker services if needed) ``` Relay on `ws://localhost:3000`. You're in. Want a single-node / VPS relay instead of the local-dev stack? Use the production Compose bundle in [`deploy/compose/`](deploy/compose/README.md) (`docker compose` + Postgres, Redis, MinIO, optional Caddy/TLS). The root [`docker-compose.yml`](docker-compose.yml) is for day-to-day development only. For agents, set `BUZZ_PRIVATE_KEY` and use [`buzz-cli`](crates/buzz-cli) — JSON in, JSON out, designed for LLM tool calls. --- ## Windows prerequisites The agent shell tool runs commands under bash. On macOS and Linux that's already there; on Windows you need to bring it. Install [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win) — it ships Git Bash, which is what buzz resolves at runtime. Once it's installed, everything works the same as on other platforms. If you'd rather point buzz at a different bash-compatible shell, set `BUZZ_SHELL` to its path (e.g. `BUZZ_SHELL=C:\path\to\bash.exe`). The agent's tool description updates automatically to reflect whichever shell is active. --- ## Architecture ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Clients │ │ Human client AI agent CLI / scripts │ │ (desktop, mobile) (Goose, Codex, ...) (buzz-cli, agents) │ │ │ ┌──────────────┐ │ │ │ │ │ buzz-acp │ │ │ │ │ │ (ACP ↔ MCP) │ │ │ │ │ └──────┬───────┘ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ └───────┼──────────────────────┼───────────────────────┼──────────────────┘ │ WebSocket │ WS + REST │ WS + REST ▼ ▼ ▼ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ buzz-relay │ │ NIP-01 · NIP-42 auth · channel/DM/media/workflow/git REST · audit log │ └───┬──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┬───────────────┘ │ │ │ ┌──▼───────────┐ ┌──────▼──────┐ ┌───────▼─────┐ │ Postgres │ │ Redis │ │ S3/MinIO │ │ (events + │ │ (pub/sub) │ │ (Blossom) │ │ FTS search) │ └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘ └──────────────┘ ``` A Rust workspace of focused crates. Single source of truth: the relay. The human clients are the desktop app in [block/buzz-app](https://github.com/block/buzz-app) and the mobile app in [`mobile/`](mobile/). See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the full breakdown.
Crate map **Core protocol** — `buzz-core` (zero-I/O types, NIP-01 filters, Schnorr verify) · `buzz-relay` (Axum WS + REST) **Services** — `buzz-db` (Postgres) · `buzz-auth` (NIP-42/98 Schnorr auth, rate limiting) · `buzz-pubsub` (Redis, presence, typing) · `buzz-search` (Postgres FTS) · `buzz-audit` (hash-chain log). Multi-community mode scopes tenant-observable rows, cache keys, search documents, workflow state, media metadata, git repo pointers, and audit chains by the host-derived community; s

[workspace.package]
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.88.0"
license = "Apache-2.0"
repository = "https://github.com/block/sprout"

[workspace.dependencies]
# Runtime
tokio       = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros", "net", "time", "sync", "io-util", "signal", "process"] }
tokio-util  = { version = "0.7", features = ["rt", "codec"] }

# HTTP + WebSocket
axum        = { version = "0.8", features = ["ws", "macros"] }
tower       = { version = "0.5", features = ["timeout", "util", "limit"] }
tower-http  = { version = "0.6", features = ["trace", "cors", "compression-gzip", "limit", "timeout", "fs"] }

# Database
sqlx = { version = "=0.9.0", features = [
    "runtime-tokio", "tls-rustls", "postgres", "uuid", "chrono", "json"
] }

# Redis
redis        = { version = "1.0", features = ["tokio-comp", "tokio-rustls-comp"] }

# crate's own rustls dependency.
kube = { version = "2.0", default-features = false, features = ["client", "rustls-tls"] }
k8s-openapi = { version = "0.26", features = ["v1_31"] }

# Nostr
nostr = { version = "0.44", features = ["nip44", "nip98"] }

# Serialization

name: airgorah
description: A WiFi security auditing software
readme_content:
Airgorah

A WiFi security auditing software

Installation    |    Usage    |    Credits

![illustration](.github/assets/illustration.png) [![crates](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/airgorah.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/airgorah) [![aur](https://img.shields.io/aur/version/airgorah)](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/airgorah) [![ci](https://github.com/martin-olivier/airgorah/actions/workflows/CI.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/martin-olivier/airgorah/actions/workflows/CI.yml) `Airgorah` is a WiFi security auditing software that can capture nearby WiFi traffic, discover clients connected to access points, perform deauthentication attacks, capture handshakes and PMKIDs, and crack the password of access points. It is written in Rust and uses [GTK4](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk4-rs) for the graphical part. `⭐ Don't forget to put a star if you like the project!` ## Legal ⚠️ Airgorah is designed to be used in testing and discovering flaws in networks you are owner of. Performing attacks on WiFi networks you are not owner of is illegal in almost all countries. I am not responsible for whatever damage you may cause by using this software. ## Requirements This software only works on `linux`. The graphical interface runs as a normal user (so it works under both `X11` and `Wayland`). When a privileged operation is needed, it launches a small privileged agent (`airgorah-agent`) via `polkit`, which will prompt for authentication once. You will also need a wireless network card that supports `monitor mode` and `packet injection`. ## Installation The installation instructions are available [here](https://github.com/martin-olivier/airgorah/wiki/Installation). ## Usage The documentation about the usage of the application is available [here](https://github.com/martin-olivier/airgorah/wiki/Usage). ## License This project is released under [MIT](LICENSE) license. ## Contributing If you have any question about the usage of the application, do not hesitate to open a [discussion](https://github.com/martin-olivier/airgorah/discussions) If you want to report a bug or provide a feature, do not hesitate to open an [issue](https://github.com/martin-olivier/airgorah/issues) or submit a [pull request](https://github.com/martin-olivier/airgorah/pulls)

> The reason your React component is re-rendering is likely because you're creating a new object reference on each render cycle. When you pass an inline object as a prop, React's shallow comparison sees it as a different object every time, which triggers a re-render. I'd recommend using useMemo to memoize the object. > New object ref each render, so React re-renders. Wrap the prop in `useMemo`.
**Same fix. 63 token become 20. Brain still big.** Pick your club: | Skill | Same answer | Tokens | |---|---|---:| | `/caveman` | New object ref each render, so React re-renders. Wrap the prop in `useMemo`. | 20 | | `/ultracave` | Inline object prop, new ref, re-render. `useMemo`. | 14 | | `/megacave` | 新參照致重繪。`useMemo`。 | **13** | Token counts: tiktoken o200k. ## Install ```bash npx @caveman-ai/cli@latest ``` One command. Only Auto needs an account, and it is free. [4.0.0 release notes](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/releases/tag/v4.0.0) ## Proof Outside labs first. Ours come with each rock below. So caveman grew rocks that shrink what the agent *reads* and what it *runs on*. ## Say less: the caveman voice **A voice, not broken grammar. Every reply follows the same structure.** | Rule | What it means | |---|---| | **Answer first** | `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].` No greeting, no "let me", no recap | | **One idea per sentence** | Built on [ASD-STE100](https://www.asd-ste100.org/), the controlled English of aircraft maintenance manuals: 20 words max, active voice, one term per thing | | **Meaning never dropped** | Articles can go. *not*, *never*, *no*, *only* never go. name: omnigraph
description: Object-storage native graph database with branching and typed ontology
readme_content:
Object-storage native graph database with branching and typed ontology.
Unified retrieval engine (vector/BM25/graph) · Git-style workflows · Open data format (Lance)

Quickstart  ·  Docs  ·  Cookbooks  ·  CLI  ·  Studio  ·  llms.txt

Omnigraph is engineered for the new workload introduced by long-horizon agents: multiple agents sharing a typed world model to continuously retrieve and update context and coordinate work. Agents and UIs can become thin stateless consumers of durable state. Omnigraph Cloud is in private preview: [join the waitlist](https://www.omnigraph.dev/cloud?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=cloud-waitlist). Join the [Omnigraph Slack community](https://join.slack.com/t/omnigraphworkspace/shared_invite/zt-3wfpglyxj-lHvJGhuySPfqLtN35uJZNw) to ask questions, share feedback, and follow development. ## Capabilities | Capability | What it gives you | |---|---| | **Typed ontology** | Agents share one enforceable model of the domain. `.pg` schemas declare node and edge types, keys and constraints, and the engine enforces them on every write. | | **Multimodal retrieval** | Agents assemble high-precision & recall context in one query: graph traversal + vector ANN + full-text + Reciprocal Rank Fusion in **one** runtime, with filtering. | | **Branching** | Agents propose reviewable changes instead of writing to main: a branch per agent or task, three-way merge, time travel across the whole graph. | | **Declared as code** | A `cluster.yaml` declares graphs, schemas, stored queries, embedding providers and policies. `cluster plan` previews, `cluster apply` converges, Terraform-style. | | **Security as code** | Cedar policy enforced **server-side on every mutation**, per graph or server-wide; bearer auth, server-resolved actors, audit tracking. | | **Object-storage native, open format** | Decoupled storage and compute. Store graphs on local disk or S3-compatible storage: RustFS / MinIO, AWS S3 / R2, or Azure preview. Graph data uses open, versioned [Lance](https://github.com/lance-format/lance), including Blob values. | ## What you can build | Use case | What it's for | |---|---| | **Company brain** | Org knowledge unified into one graph every agent can query | | **Agentic memory** | Durable, versioned memory: a branch per agent or per task, merged on review | | **Context graph** | Decision traces and codified tribal knowledge for retrieval | | **Dev graph** | Issues & dependency model that coding agents read and write | | **R&D / ML data layer** | Experiments and trials written into branches, versioned for training & eval | ## Install ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph/main/scripts/install.sh | bash ``` This installs `omnigraph` (CLI) and `omnigraph-server` into `~/.local/bin` from published release binaries. Or with Homebrew: ```bash brew tap ModernRelay/tap brew install ModernRelay/tap/omnigraph ``` ## Studio [Omnigraph Studio](https://www.omnigraph.dev/studio?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=studio) is the desktop app for your graphs. Browse each type as a table, follow relationships on a canvas, write queries with the compiler's errors as you type, and review what a branch changes before you merge it. It is a native Rust app on GPUI, the framework behind Zed, for macOS, Windows and Linux. Open a graph on one of your server targets in Studio: ```bash omnigraph studio --target --graph ``` [Download Studio](https://www.omnigraph.dev/studio?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=studio) or read [its source](https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph-studio). ## Set it up with an AI agent Omnigraph is built to be run by coding agents. Two ways in: **Teach your agent the playbook.** The `omnigraph` binary carries the [**`omnigraph` agent skill**](skills/omnigraph) written for it: the operational playbook covering cluster mode, the two config surfaces, schema evolution, query linting, data writes, branches, Cedar policy, and the common gotchas. Export it where your agent loads skills, so the skill always matches the installed CLI: ```bash omnigraph skill export ~/.claude/skills/omnigraph --force ``` With an older CLI that has no `skill` command, or none installed, `npx skills add ModernRelay/omnigraph@omnigraph` installs the copy on the default branch instead. **Or have an agent set it up from scratch.** Paste this into Claude Code, Codex, or any agent that can read a URL and run a shell command: ```text Read https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph/blob/main/skills/omnigraph/references/onboarding.md and follow it to set up Omnigraph for me. ``` The agent installs the CLI, asks what the graph is for, builds and queries a small local graph, and then points to the cookbooks, a cluster or Omnigraph Cloud. For ready-to-run graphs with real seed data (company brain, VC operating system, pharma & industry intel), [`ModernRelay/omnigraph-cookbooks`](https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph-cookbooks) is the fastest way to see Omnigraph shaped to a real domain. ## Deploy A **cluster** declares graphs, schemas, stored queries, and policies in a configuration bundle. `cluster plan` previews changes and `cluster apply` submits them to the selected destination. The cluster-only HTTP server exposes graphs at `/graphs/{id}/…` and activates applied changes without a restart. Keep desired configuration separate from its destination: ``` company-brain/ ├── cluster.yaml ├── people.pg # schema for the "knowledge" graph ├── queries/ # stored queries: the .gq files ARE the declaration │ └── people.gq ├── cluster.policy.yaml # deployment permissions └── graph.policy.yaml # graph permissions ``` ```yaml # cluster.yaml version: 1 metadata: name: company-brain graphs: knowledge: schema: people.pg queries: queries/ # every `query ` in queries/*.gq registers policies: cluster-access: file: cluster.policy.yaml applies_to: [cluster] graph-access: file: graph.policy.yaml applies_to: [knowledge] ``` For first boot, follow the [cluster guide](docs/user/clusters/index.md#bootstrap-a-cluster), including writer ownership transfer and authentication. The [deployment guide](docs/user/deployment.md) covers containers and object stores; Azure writers require its admission wrapper. The applied cluster policy must grant the authenticated operator `config_manage`. Schema changes also require `read` and `schema_apply` on the affected graphs. With those grants and a server target named `production`, deploy local edits: ```bash omnigraph cluster validate --config ./company-brain omnigraph cluster plan --target production --config ./company-brain omnigraph cluster apply --target production --config ./company-brain ``` `--config` names the source bundle; `--target` names the destination. Omitting `storage` from the bundle uses the selected destination's root. If present, `storage` must match that root; it never selects or redirects the target. Apply prints a deployment ID. If delivery is interrupted, inspect that ID before submitting again; see [deployment recovery](docs/user/clusters/index.md). ## Query and mutate Define a server target with `default_graph` and set `defaults.target` once in `~/.omnigraph/config.yaml` ([configuration](docs/user/cli/index.md)), and the everyday commands stay short. Stored queries and mutations run **by name**: ```bash omnigraph query search_docs --params '{"q":"AI safety"}' omnigraph mutate add_person --params '{"name":"Mina"}' ``` Branch, review and merge across the whole graph, so agents write in isolation: ```bash omnigraph branch create --from main agent/ingest-42 omnigraph branch merge agent/ingest-42 --into main ``` An **alias** is shorter still: bind a target, graph, and stored query to one name, then `omnigraph alias triage` runs it. Data commands use `--target NAME` for a configured server or managed resource, plus `--graph ID` when needed. Use `--target ./graph.omni` for a standalone local graph. Control-plane login and organization operations use `--profile`; see [operator configuration](docs/user/cli/targets.md). ## Security & governance - **Engine-wide enforcement:** every write path goes through the same Cedar gate, so the HTTP server, the CLI, and the embedded SDK obey identical rules. - **Declared in the cluster:** a policy bundle is bound to graphs (or the whole server) via `policies:` → `applies_to`. - **Scoped:** rules apply per graph, per branch, or server-wide. - **Static server credentials:** static bearer tokens are hashed at startup and compared in constant time. - **Forge-proof identity:** the actor is resolved server-side from the token; clients can't set it. See the [policy guide](docs/user/operations/policy.md). ## Clients & SDKs | Client | Use it for | Where | |---|---|---| | **TypeScript SDK** | typed access from Node / TS | [`@modernrelay/omnigraph`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@modernrelay/omnigraph) · [source](https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph-ts) | | **Built-in MCP** | connect an agent to the server's `/mcp`, directly or through `omnigraph mcp --target NAME` | [MCP guide](docs/user/operations/mcp.md) | | **Omnigraph Studio** | browse, query and review a graph in a desktop app | [download](https://www.omnigraph.dev/studio?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=studio) · [source](https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph-studio) | | **HTTP / OpenAPI** | use the wire contract from any language | [HTTP guide](docs/user/operations/server.md) · [OpenAPI](openapi.json) | Match the client's HTTP contract to the server's. The 0.14 server requires contract `0.14`; see [client availability](docs/user/install.md#client-compatibility) before selecting an npm package. ## Docs - [0.14 highlights and upgrade actions](docs/releases/v0.14.0-overview.md) · [User guide](docs/user/index.md) - [Cluster guide](docs/user/clusters/index.md) · [Deployment guide](docs/user/deployment.md) · [CLI reference](docs/user/cli/reference.md) - [Schema](docs/user/schema/index.md) · [Queries](docs/user/queries/index.md) · [Search](docs/user/search/index.md) · [Policy](docs/user/operations/policy.md) ## Build and test ```bash cargo build --workspace --locked cargo test --workspac

readme_content:
# OpenBot ### AI coworkers. Ready for the enterprise. A modular, self-hostable workspace for AI coworkers.
Choose your models. Bring your agents. Own your infrastructure. [open.bot](https://open.bot) · [Docs](docs/README.md) · [Deploy on Kubernetes](#deploy-on-kubernetes) · [Run from source](#run-from-source) [![GitHub Trending: #3 Repository Of The Day](https://trendshift.io/api/badge/repositories/175080)](https://trendshift.io/repositories/175080) [![Trendshift: #3 Repository Of The Day](https://trendshift.io/api/badge/trendshift/repositories/175080/daily)](https://trendshift.io/repositories/175080)
[![Download for Mac (Apple silicon)](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/CopilotKit/OpenBot?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=3A3466&logo=data%3Aimage%2Fsvg%2Bxml%3Bbase64%2CPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCAyNCAyNCI%2BPHBhdGggZmlsbD0iI2ZmZiIgZD0iTTExIDNoMnYxMC4ybDMuNi0zLjZMMTggMTFsLTYgNi02LTYgMS40LTEuNCAzLjYgMy42ek01IDE5aDE0djJINXoiLz48L3N2Zz4%3D&label=Download%20for%20Mac%20%28Apple%20silicon%29&color=6E6AE0)](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-arm64.dmg) [![Download for Mac (Intel)](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/CopilotKit/OpenBot?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=3A3466&logo=data%3Aimage%2Fsvg%2Bxml%3Bbase64%2CPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCAyNCAyNCI%2BPHBhdGggZmlsbD0iI2ZmZiIgZD0iTTExIDNoMnYxMC4ybDMuNi0zLjZMMTggMTFsLTYgNi02LTYgMS40LTEuNCAzLjYgMy42ek01IDE5aDE0djJINXoiLz48L3N2Zz4%3D&label=Download%20for%20Mac%20%28Intel%29&color=4A7CC8)](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-x64.dmg) [![Download for Windows](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/CopilotKit/OpenBot?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=3A3466&logo=data%3Aimage%2Fsvg%2Bxml%3Bbase64%2CPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCAyNCAyNCI%2BPHBhdGggZmlsbD0iI2ZmZiIgZD0iTTExIDNoMnYxMC4ybDMuNi0zLjZMMTggMTFsLTYgNi02LTYgMS40LTEuNCAzLjYgMy42ek01IDE5aDE0djJINXoiLz48L3N2Zz4%3D&label=Download%20for%20Windows&color=9A5CC6)](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-windows-x64-setup.exe) Notarized .dmg for Apple silicon and Intel Macs · signed installer for Windows x64 · no terminal or developer tools needed · [Release notes](https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot/releases/latest)
[![OpenBot for Business: get early access](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenBot_for_Business-Get_early_access_%E2%86%92-D14B9C?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=3A3466)](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) From [CopilotKit](https://www.copilotkit.ai), creators of [AG-UI](https://github.com/ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui).
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c60f07da-8b6d-46eb-a573-17fc1e65a644

Watch a Bot use its browser and tools, answer with interactive results, and wait for your approval before it sends. Take over when it needs you, and connect the agents you already run.

## Getting started ### On your laptop The easiest way to get started is with the fully self-contained app that runs on your laptop, combining the OpenBot frontend and Docker-based backend in one application. [Mac / Apple silicon](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-arm64.dmg) · [Mac / Intel](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-x64.dmg) · [Windows](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-windows-x64-setup.exe) [Run from source](#run-from-source) ### For your team **OpenBot for Business** brings your agents into one workspace with company sign-in, tool permissions, approvals, and audit. Deploy on your infrastructure or work with our engineers on hosting and customization. [**Get early access to OpenBot for Business →**](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [**Talk to an engineer**](https://open.bot/business) · [**Kubernetes setup**](#deploy-on-kubernetes) ### Web, mobile, and chat [Web](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=web&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [iOS](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=ios&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Android](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=android&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Slack](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=slack&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Teams](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=teams&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) ## Your workspace. Your stack.
- **Choose your models.** Use OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, or open models through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, hosted by a provider or on your own infrastructure. Keep your provider relationships and change models as your needs change. - **Bring your agents.** Run built-in Bots in the OpenBot server, or connect your existing agents through AG-UI from any agent execution platform. Agents built with different stacks can work in the same workspace. - **Make it yours.** Use the MIT-licensed template as-is, white-label it, or customize it deeply. AG-UI connects agents, MCP connects tools, and the frontends and backend can evolve independently. - **Govern work across your team.** Company sign-in, roles, tool permissions, approvals, and audit apply across the workspace. Your agents use OpenBot's tools and computers under the same policies. - **Get help deploying it.** CopilotKit's engineers can work with your team to deploy OpenBot, connect your systems, and automate parts of specific jobs. [Connect your agent](#bring-your-own-agent) · [Configure models and tools](docs/configuration.md) · [Explore OpenBot for Business](https://open.bot/business) ## Built on CopilotKit and AG-UI OpenBot is built on [CopilotKit](https://www.copilotkit.ai), which is [used in production by a majority of Fortune 500 companies](https://www.copilotkit.ai/blog/series-a). **Your agent stack.** [AG-UI](https://docs.ag-ui.com/introduction#supported-integrations) has first-class integrations across the major agent frameworks and harnesses, including Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK, Microsoft Agent Framework and Agent Harness, Google ADK, AWS Strands, Oracle Agent Spec, LangChain, Mastra, Pydantic AI, Agno, and CrewAI. Many ship first-party support; [Amazon Bedrock AgentCore supports AG-UI directly](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-agui.html). **Your execution platform.** Keep your agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Claude Managed Agents, [Google's Agent Platform](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform), LangChain's Managed Deep Agents, [Microsoft Foundry Agent Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agents), or your own infrastructure. Connect them to OpenBot through an AG-UI endpoint, using an adapter where needed. Your choice of agent platform stays independent of your workspace. ## Architecture OpenBot has three parts. On your laptop, setup runs the backend and Intelligence for you. For a team, the Helm chart deploys both on Kubernetes in your own infrastructure. | Part | What it does | | --- | --- | | **OpenBot frontends** | Mac, Windows, web, iOS, Android, Slack, and Teams connect people to the same workspace. Conversations, interactive results, computer view, and approvals adapt to each surface. [Choose a frontend](#getting-started). | | **OpenBot backend** | Runs the workspace API and built-in Bots, connects external agents and tools, manages Bot computers, and enforces identity, permissions, action policies, and audit. Deploys on Kubernetes with PostgreSQL and persistent storage. | | **CopilotKit Intelligence** | Durable conversations, memory, Automatic Learning, and enterprise governance services. Separately licensed; runs on Kubernetes alongside OpenBot. | OpenBot enforces sign-in, tool permissions, action policies, and audit at its API, alongside Intelligence's platform services. Built-in Bots run in the OpenBot server; your own agents can run alongside OpenBot or on any agent execution platform. Both use AG-UI and can share the same workspace. Computer execution is pluggable: use the default Kubernetes setup or connect a compatible external computer provider. [Architecture details](docs/architecture.md) · [Services and ports](#services-and-ports) · [Kubernetes deployment](#deploy-on-kubernetes) ## Open source, local operation, and licensing **The OpenBot application template is open source under the [MIT license](LICENSE).** You can fork, modify, and white-label it. It uses **CopilotKit Intelligence**, which is separately licensed and can run entirely on your own machine or infrastructure. | Where you run it | CopilotKit Intelligence license | | --- | --- | | **Your laptop, for personal use and experimentation** | Requires a free local Intelligence license. Desktop setup handles this for you. | | **Kubernetes evaluation** | Requires a free Intelligence trial license. [Request a trial](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access). | | **Kubernetes / production** | Requires a production Intelligence license beyond evaluation. OpenBot for Business includes Intelligence for use with OpenBot. [Plans and pricing](https://open.bot/pricing). | **Fully local is an option.** Run OpenBot, Intelligence, and a compatible model locally. A cloud model or connected online app still sends requests to that service. Initial downloads, account sign-in, and local license renewal need internet access. --- ## Deploy on Kubernetes Deploy OpenBot and CopilotKit Intelligence together on **AWS EKS, Azure AKS, Google GKE, or your own Kubernetes cluster**. The chart installs Intelligence by default; no separate hosted project is required. For a first evaluation, you need a cluster with **amd64 nodes**, a **default StorageClass**, `kubectl`, Helm, a **trial or production license**, and a model key. The commands below use an OpenAI key. For Anthropic, a model router, cluster sizing, or an existing Intelligence deployment, use the full Helm guide that comes with the chart (`helm show readme` on the chart below). > **Setting up with an AI assistant?** Give it this README and the Helm guide (`helm show readme` on the chart below).
